requirement: Eager/lazy script initialization and source discovery are explicit

obligations.note: preload() resolves eagerly, at the time subject.gd itself is loaded -- not deferred to when Preloaded is first used
never reached: the load()-using branch is not taken

notes: The sharpest test of eager-vs-lazy is expected_resource_cache in uses_preloaded, checked by pilot/fixtures/driver.gd directly (not by comparator.py, same category as expected_log): ResourceLoader.has_cached() on dependency.gd's path is false before subject.gd is ever loaded, and already TRUE immediately after subject.gd loads -- before run() is ever called, and specifically for the input where the load()-using branch (line 7) is never taken. This proves preload() resolves at parse time of the FILE THAT CONTAINS IT, not at first use, and not dependent on which branches execute. load() by contrast is a plain statement (line 7) that only resolves when actually reached, matching the uses_loaded input where line 7 is hit and line 9 (the preloaded path) is not. Confirmed on the pinned Godot 4.7.1 engine via pilot/fixtures/driver.gd.
